## Solution

**Setup and notation.** Let $(M, g)$ be a Riemannian manifold with Ricci curvature tensor $\mathrm{Ric}_{ij}$ (a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor). Let $\omega = \omega_i\, dx^i$ be a 1-form. The metric $g$ induces the musical isomorphism $\sharp : T^*M \to TM$, converting the 1-form $\omega$ into the vector field
$$
\omega^\sharp = g^{ij}\omega_j\,\partial_i, \qquad (\omega^\sharp)^j = g^{ji}\omega_i.
$$

**Definition of $\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)$.** The natural action of the Ricci tensor on a 1-form is: convert $\omega$ to the vector field $\omega^\sharp$, then contract the Ricci tensor with this vector field on one slot, producing a 1-form:
$$
\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)_k \;=\; \mathrm{Ric}_{jk}\,(\omega^\sharp)^j \;=\; \mathrm{Ric}_{jk}\,g^{ji}\,\omega_i.
$$

**Raising an index.** The contraction $\mathrm{Ric}_{jk}\,g^{ji}$ raises the first index of the Ricci tensor, giving the **Ricci operator** (the Ricci endomorphism), the $(1,1)$-tensor
$$
\mathrm{Ric}^{\,i}{}_{k} \;=\; g^{ji}\,\mathrm{Ric}_{jk}.
$$
(Equivalently $\mathrm{Ric}^{\,i}{}_{k} = g^{ij}\mathrm{Ric}_{jk}$, using the symmetry $\mathrm{Ric}_{jk}=\mathrm{Ric}_{kj}$.)

**Substituting back:**
$$
\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)_k \;=\; \mathrm{Ric}^{\,i}{}_{k}\,\omega_i.
$$

This is precisely the action of the $(1,1)$-tensor $\mathrm{Ric}^{\,i}{}_{k}$ on the 1-form $\omega$ — i.e., the Ricci operator applied to $\omega$.

**Conclusion.** We have shown
$$
\boxed{\mathrm{Ric}(\omega) \;=\; \mathrm{Ric}\cdot\omega,}
$$
where the factor $A$ is the **Ricci operator** — the $(1,1)$-tensor obtained by raising one index of the Ricci curvature tensor via the metric:
$$
A \;=\; \mathrm{Ric}^{\,i}{}_{j} \;=\; g^{ik}\,\mathrm{Ric}_{kj}.
$$

In words: $A$ is the Ricci curvature tensor with one index raised by the inverse metric (the Ricci endomorphism / Ricci operator).
